# Wavelength-Selective Switch

`maiman.components.WavelengthSelectiveSwitch` · category **Passive** · [all components](index.md)

A ROADM's add/drop degree: one channel off the line, a new one on in its place.

`in` is the line arriving at the node, `add` the local transmitter. Every
channel of the line but `dropped` leaves by `out` through its own
passband (express); the `dropped` channel leaves by `drop` through its
passband, and whatever arrives on `add` in that slot takes its place on
`out`.

**The switch does not block perfectly.** `isolation` is how far below its
arrival the dropped channel still reaches `out`, and there it lands on the
added channel's own frequency: in-band crosstalk, which no filter
downstream can remove. The two are added as fields, so the leak beats with
the new channel at the receiver -- the reason a node's isolation is
specified at 35 dB or more, far beyond a demultiplexer's neighbour
rejection.

The passband of every port is the demultiplexer's, on the same grid, so a
channel off the plan is attenuated by the skirt rather than special-cased.

## Ports

| Port | Direction | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `in` | input | optical |
| `add` | input | optical |
| `out` | output | optical |
| `drop` | output | optical |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `first_wavelength` | `1550.0` | nm | 1200.0 … 1700.0 | Channel 0. The rest are stepped from it up in frequency, down in wavelength |
| `spacing` | `100.0` | GHz | 1.0 …  | Channel spacing, in frequency because the grid is |
| `wavelength_spacing` | `0.0` | nm | 0.0 …  | A coarse grid's step in wavelength (CWDM: 20 nm), replacing `spacing`; 0 is off |
| `bandwidth` | `50.0` | GHz | 0.0 …  | 3 dB full width of each channel's passband |
| `order` | `3.0` |  | 1.0 … 10.0 | Super-Gaussian order; 3 to 5 is an AWG |
| `insertion_loss` | `4.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Loss per channel. An AWG routes, so this does not grow with the count |
| `extinction` | `40.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Out-of-band rejection floor; 0 disables the floor |
| `dropped` | `1.0` |  | 0.0 …  | The channel dropped and re-added, counted from 0 |
| `isolation` | `35.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | How far below its arrival the dropped channel still leaks to `out` |

## Constructor arguments

Set when the block is created, not swept: `channels`.
